End-to-End Differentiable Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics for Fluid--Rigid Optimization with Gradient Stabilization
abstract: We introduce an end-to-end differentiable optimization framework for Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) with fluid–rigid body coupling. The central difficulty is not only to obtain local derivatives of SPH operators, but also to propagate useful sensitivities through long rollouts whose particle neighborhoods, contacts, and pressure responses change rapidly over time. These effects make reverse-mode gradients noisy and often cause adjoint variables to explode in long-horizon control and inverse-design tasks. We formulate an SPH-specific reverse-mode pipeline for IISPH-based fluid–rigid simulation and implement the required vector–Jacobian products within checkpointed simulation segments. To make the resulting gradients usable for optimization, we introduce a self-adaptive adjoint correction sequence that acts as a descent-preserving preconditioner: it bounds pathological adjoint amplification while keeping the update direction aligned with the original reverse-mode sensitivity. Our experiments cover a sequence of increasingly demanding tasks, from low-dimensional impulse and shape optimization to scalar-amplitude water actuation, multi-object water-jet balancing, and neural fluid-mediated pendulum control. These results demonstrate that stabilized reverse-mode differentiation can support challenging SPH-based optimization problems involving indirect momentum transfer, long-horizon event timing, and high-dimensional control.

title: Consistency-Aware Map Generation at Multiple Zoom Levels Using Aerial Image
abstract: The multi-level tiled map service is widely used and serves as a kind of digital infrastructure. These map tiles are usually rendered from vector data, whose update needs to walk or drive with professional equipment to check every points of interest. This leads to inconvenience and expensive cost in timely updating maps. Compared with vector data, aerial images are much easier and cheaper to obtain. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-level map generation framework that can automatically generate accurate and consistent maps with multiple zoom levels from aerial images. It consists of a level-aware map generator and a consistency-aware map generator. The level-aware map generator is able to generate accurate initial maps with realistic details for each zoom level. The consistency-aware map generator regards initial maps at each zoom level as a sequence and builds the connection between them, so as to guarantee content consistency between maps at different zoom levels. Furthermore, we collect a large-scale high-quality dataset called Multi-Level Map (MLM) for map generation at multiple zoom levels. Experiments on our MLM dataset show that our method outperforms previous state-of-the-art map generation methods on both comprehensive quantitative metrics and perceptual quality.

title: Over-the-Air Semantic Alignment via Dual Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces
abstract: Semantic communications enable task-oriented information exchange, but suffer from latent-space mismatch when transmitter and receiver employ heterogeneous machine learning models. Existing semantic alignment methods rely on digital processing, introducing computational and latency overhead. This paper proposes a dual stacked intelligent metasurfaces (dual-SIM) architecture that performs semantic alignment entirely in the wave domain. By jointly exploiting programmable metasurfaces at both ends of a link and the wireless channel, the proposed architecture realizes an end-to-end linear transformation between heterogeneous latent spaces. We show phase-only multilayer SIM can approximate both supervised linear aligners and zero-shot Parseval-frame equalizers. We investigate single-SIM, disjoint asymmetric and symmetric dual-SIM, and jointly optimized dual-SIM configurations, considering channel equalization and constructive channel exploitation. For joint design, we develop an alternating projected gradient algorithm with convergence guarantees to first-order stationary points. We further introduce a deep-unrolled network that unrolls gradient-based iterations to reduce computational cost of SIM reconfiguration under channel variations. Numerical results with heterogeneous vision transformer encoders show accurate semantic alignment from moderate to high signal-to-noise ratios. The joint and symmetric disjoint dual-SIM designs achieve the highest accuracy over compact channels, the joint design leads at shallow stack depths, and the advantage over single-SIM designs diminishes at equal depth.

title: PALIN: Pixel-Aligned LiDAR-NIR Multimodal 3D Object Detection with Benchmark
abstract: 3D object detection is critical for intelligent transportation systems. LiDAR has been widely adopted for accurate geometric measurements; however, purely geometric representations remain ambiguous under sparse observations and occlusions, while cross-sensor multimodal fusion suffers from calibration and synchronization errors. To overcome these challenges, we leverage an Ouster LiDAR to construct PALIN (Pixel-Aligned LiDAR-NIR), a large-scale intrinsically pixel-aligned multimodal dataset jointly capturing geometry and NIR intensity, comprising approximately 8,000 annotated frames from static urban intersections and diverse mobile suburban scenes. Building upon this dataset, we propose CMambaFusion, a novel fusion framework consisting of a four-directional Cross-Mamba module for bidirectional cross-modal interaction and a Gated Concat-Mamba module for joint feature refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PALIN enables effective multimodal learning, and CMambaFusion achieves superior accuracy-efficiency trade-offs over both LiDAR-only and representative fusion baselines.

title: InvarOrd: Self-Supervised Ordinal Knowledge Distillation with Rank-Invariant Alignment for Label-Efficient Cross-Species Hyperspectral Fish Freshness Assessment
abstract: Hyperspectral models of fish freshness rarely transfer between species, and labelling a new species is slow and destructive. Freshness is also ordinal, and standard domain alignment can erase that order. We present InvarOrd, which adapts to a new species from 30 labelled cubes (5 per rank) in three stages: self-supervised spectral pretraining on unlabelled source cubes, cross-species alignment by a shrinkage covariance discrepancy computed only within matched ranks, and ordinal distillation into a compact student. The alignment term is provably invariant to the rank means, so it gives no incentive to collapse the ordinal axis. On paired salmon and cod data (800 cubes each, 16 days), a source-trained teacher reaches 1.6 to 1.9 days mean absolute error (MAE) on the other species, with quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) below zero. The 423K-parameter student, 2.54 times smaller than its teacher, attains the lowest MAE (1.476 days) and highest within 1-day accuracy (56.1%) among 14 configurations, matching the best of six ImageNet-pretrained backbones (ConvNeXt-T, 1.503 days) at 66 times fewer parameters, 1.44ms per cube on a GPU and 5s re-adaptation. InvarOrd beats target-only training by 0.29 days (p = 0.031). Among alignment objectives, rank-invariant alignment retains the most ordinal structure (embedding rank correlation 0.183, QWK 0.112), whereas global discrepancy lowers the rank correlation to 0.049 and QWK to zero at only 0.014 days higher MAE.

title: Detecting Small Space Objects for Space Situational Awareness with Collaborative Edge AI
abstract: With the rapid growth of space activities, near-Earth space is becoming increasingly congested, leading to a higher risk of spacecraft collisions and space debris generation. Recent close-proximity encounters and collision incidents necessitate efficient and cost-effective onboard systems for space object detection (SOD) and collision avoidance. While deep learning (DL) enabled Edge AI using low-cost vision sensors on single or multiple satellites has shown promises for SOD, significant challenges remain, including limited datasets, small SOD, and the lack of comprehensive performance assessments. This paper presents a collaborative Edge AI framework for multiview SOD and systematically benchmarks DL models and fusion strategies. Results show that higher image resolution significantly improves small SOD. For multiple views, image-level fusion reduces the combined communication and inference latency by 30.13% and 32.80% on average compared with feature-level and attention-based fusion across the evaluated inter-satellite link (ISL) bandwidth. For larger view sets, feature-level and attention-based fusion achieve better detection accuracy at the cost of analysis in the sensing-communication pipeline, revealing that multiview collaboration introduces minimal latency overhead under ISL constraints when reception capacity is not exceeded. Our work provides valuable design insights for future collaborative satellite network design, supporting the emerging space situational awareness and space traffic management requirements.

title: XLSAR-Bench: Towards Extremely Large SAR Imagery Understanding of MLLMs
abstract: The rapid development of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) has highlighted the need for comprehensive benchmarks to assess their capabilities and limitations in remote sensing (RS). However, evaluating MLLMs in large-size synthetic aperture radar (SAR) scenarios remains challenging, as understanding complete scenes requires both global semantic interpretation and fine-grained target perception. Existing SAR benchmarks predominantly rely on small image patches, limiting their ability to assess these capabilities jointly. To address these limitations, we present XLSAR-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating the perception and reasoning capabilities of MLLMs in large-scene SAR imagery. XLSAR-Bench comprises 405 images with an average size of 7153$\times$7153 pixels, ten tasks spanning visual question answering, visual grounding, and detailed image captioning, with all evaluation samples meticulously annotated manually, assisted by a semi-automatic captioner. Experimental results from general-purpose and domain-specific MLLMs reveal persistent challenges in understanding large SAR scenes and accurately perceiving small targets. We have open-sourced XLSAR-Bench to support further research in developing more powerful MLLMs for complete large SAR scenes.

title: SAR-TopoGuard: Training-Free, Speckle-Aware Topological Verification for Structure-Preserving SAR-to-Optical Translation
abstract: SAR-to-optical translators often synthesize detail that the radar measurement does not support, and pixel metrics alone cannot reveal it. We propose SAR-TopoGuard, a training-free inference-time layer for frozen generators: a stochastic sampler draws K candidates (Monte Carlo dropout for GANs, seed variance for diffusion), a speckle-aware verifier ranks them by gradient-magnitude correlation with the SAR input and a hallucination-frequency index, and a SAR-guided frequency gate admits high-frequency detail only where SAR edges support it. With all five hyperparameters frozen and three training seeds, we evaluate on 500 scene-disjoint SEN1-2 test patches, 500 patches of a held-out summer scene, and 200 cross-dataset SEN12MS winter pairs. The layer improves Pix2Pix by +0.060, +0.012, and +0.077 dB PSNR and by +0.0034, +0.0057, and +0.0135 SSIM, respectively (Wilcoxon p < 1e-6), and it improves CycleGAN and CUT on all three sets (+0.013 to +0.076 dB). It raises edge precision at the cost of edge recall (edge F1 -1.3% on the test set). On the latent diffusion model COP-GEN, it adds +0.33 dB (base) and +0.16 dB (Beta) on the winter set, the only set with dual-polarization SAR. An ablation shows that the gate produces the gain for MC-dropout GANs, whose candidates are nearly identical, whereas verifier selection contributes up to +0.26 dB for diffusion, whose samples differ. The layer has zero trainable parameters and adds 0.4 ms per patch beyond the K=5 generator passes.

title: Attribution-Guided Shared-Private Decoupling for Noise-Reduced Audio-Visual Representation Learning
abstract: Audio-visual representation learning commonly aligns paired audio and visual signals with sample-level contrastive objectives. However, real-world audio-visual pairs usually contain heterogeneous patch tokens: only a subset carries reliable cross-modal shared semantics, while many others mainly encode modality-private residuals. Aggregating all tokens into a single global representation can therefore introduce semantic noise into cross-modal alignment. Motivated by the minimal-sufficiency principle, we propose an attribution-guided shared-private decoupling framework to mitigate this issue. Our key idea is to identify shared-cover subviews that preserve dominant cross-modal information while suppressing modality-private residuals, and use them to supervise decoupled shared and private representations. To identify such subviews efficiently, we draw on transformer attribution method and introduce Layer-Truncated Attribution (LTA), which provides a lightweight estimate of token-level relevance to cross-modal shared information. We further adopt a teacher-student framework, where the teacher provides attribution-induced supervision and the student internalizes shared-private decoupling into its representations, without introducing extra inference cost. Experiments on retrieval, classification, and sound-prompted semantic segmentation show consistent gains over strong baselines. Compared with baseline, our method improves the average zero-shot R@1 by 4.0 across AudioSet and VGGSound retrieval, and improves AS20K classification mAP by 3.1, demonstrating the effectiveness of fine grained attribution guidance for reducing semantic noise.reducing semantic noise. Code will be released at https://github.com/wanglg20/LTA

title: Puzzle: One Pass Is Not Enough for Open-Vocabulary Remote Sensing Segmentation
abstract: Open-vocabulary remote sensing image segmentation (OVRSIS) enables the segmentation of unseen classes without additional annotation or retraining. By analyzing the predictions of existing OVRSIS methods, we find that many misclassified patches coexist with visually similar, correctly classified patches of the same class within the same image. Unfortunately, most of these methods stop after a single inference rather than using their predictions to guide further inference. Motivated by this observation, we propose \textbf{Puzzle}, a plug-and-play iterative re-inference framework that combines prediction history with a visual-similarity prior to progressively refine patch-level attention. Puzzle employs a lightweight history-conditioned controller to regulate each patch's contribution as an information source and its reliance on visually similar patches, while an adaptive stopping rule determines when to stop. It keeps the segmentation model frozen and reuses the same controller across different models and datasets without retraining. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent performance improvements across diverse OVRSIS models and datasets, highlighting the strong transferability of Puzzle. Moreover, Puzzle can further improve the performance of SOTA methods.

title: FDAM: A Frequency-Direction-Aware Multi-Task Framework for Pavement Crack Grid Localization
abstract: Pavement crack grid localization remains challenging for thin and tiny cracks due to weak visual cues and background interference. Box detection often misses these cracks, while supervised semantic segmentation faces limited pixel-wise annotations and high labeling costs. In this paper, we propose a Frequency-Direction-Aware Multi-Task framework (FDAM) with box detection and grid classification branches. The core grid classification branch comprises Frequency-Domain Enhancement (FDE) and Directional Feature Refinement (DFR). FDE adaptively weights spectral bands and fuses reconstructed features with spatial features. DFR captures thin crack patterns through multi-scale strip convolutions, direction-sensitive modulation, and feature recalibration. Sparse positive cells and ambiguous local predictions motivate adaptive grid supervision. Adaptive Importance Reweighting emphasizes uncertain predictions and local label transitions, with focal supervision for all cells. Our contribution is to couple the box detection and grid classification branches through shared feature learning for pavement crack grid localization. We validate FDAM on our RoadDistress2026 dataset of thin and tiny cracks and further evaluate it on public datasets Crack500 and DeepCrack. The code is available at https://github.com/Lab-PANbin/FDAM

title: Hyperspectral remote sensing of cover crop traits for decision support in precision nitrogen management
abstract: Spaceborne hyperspectral sensors offer opportunities to quantify crop traits and inform variable rate nitrogen management, yet their operational use remains limited. We evaluated PRISMA and EMIT imagery across four winter cover crop seasons in Maryland, U.S., to predict traits required by the open source Cover Crop Nitrogen Calculator (CC-NCALC) decision support tool. Traits included aboveground biomass, nitrogen concentration (N%), non-structural carbohydrates (NSC%), holocellulose (HCL%), and lignin (LIG%). Using these traits as inputs, the CC-NCALC estimates nitrogen credits from cover crops based on decomposition dynamics informed by trait data, soil, and weather conditions. Nitrogen credits are the estimated amount of plant available nitrogen that a cover crop contributes to the subsequently planted cash crop. Trait models were developed using partial least squares regression with several cross validation strategies. Biomass ( R 2 = 0.70–0.87; RMSE = 661–951 kg ha −1 ), NSC% ( R 2 = 0.69–0.72; RMSE = 4.53–7.63%), and HCL% ( R 2 = 0.65–0.70; RMSE = 5.04–7.50%) predictions were strong. But HCL% and NSC% predictions degraded under cross-scene and cross-species validation ( R 2 = 0.47–0.54; RMSE = 6.06–9.18%). N% ( R 2 = 0.15–0.79; RMSE = 0.46–0.74%) and LIG% ( R 2 = 0.02–0.35; RMSE = 1.22–1.83%) predictions were more variable; predictions using EMIT were more accurate than predictions using PRISMA, but both approaches demonstrated the need for further increases in accuracies of retrieval approaches for these two traits. Spring trait maps from April 2024 were ingested into the CC-NCALC to estimate nitrogen credits, which ranged from −14.58 to 45.65 kg N ha −1 , with higher values associated with greater legume biomass. Inter-scene comparisons demonstrate EMIT's increased spectral fidelity and trait prediction accuracy compared to PRISMA. Results demonstrate that integrating spaceborne hyperspectral imagery with decision support systems can generate site-specific nitrogen credit maps, advancing hyperspectral remote sensing toward operational nutrient management. Future missions will be critical to help scale these approaches for routine on-farm use.

title: Spatiotemporal variability in seasonal and interannual InSAR-derived excess ground ice content retrievals using Sentinel-1
abstract: The melting of excess ground ice in ice-rich permafrost regions causes elevated ground subsidence through soil thaw consolidation at landscape scales. The increased subsidence due to melting of excess ice is unaccounted for in current InSAR-based retrievals of season thaw depth, or active layer thickness (ALT); this omission may lead to overapproximated ALT estimates compared to in situ. We processed Sentinel-1 interferometric data spanning 2018–2023 over the Drew Point and Teshekpuk Lake region. Using a novel degree-day of thaw regression on InSAR displacement time series, we estimated total seasonal subsidence and found elevated subsidence during warmer years which we attribute to the melting of excess ice. Integrating these seasonal subsidence estimates into the remotely sensed active layer thickness (ReSALT) algorithm yielded consistently overapproximated ALT estimates. In conjunction with independent estimates of ALT, we exploited this positive bias in ReSALT to estimate excess ice within the active layer. We found agreement between InSAR estimates of excess ice and in situ measurements within uncertainty for warmer years. We observed a positive spatial correlation between seasonal subsidence and excess ice in the active layer with proximity to surface hydrological features. Furthermore, we observed that InSAR-derived subsidence decreases with older drained lakes, and InSAR-derived excess ice decreases with increasingly degraded ice wedge polygon type. We discovered that thaw season intensity has a first order effect on the temporal variability of seasonal subsidence and excess ice content, and the success of our method is contingent upon warm thaw seasons.

title: High resolution sediment-specific surface soil moisture retrieval using Sentinel-1 time series and auxiliary data
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: In this study, we examine the potential of continuous ground moisture monitoring over a mining site using a combination of in-situ soil moisture sensors and multi-sensor SAR images. We focus on assessing and improving methodologies for retrieval of surface soil moisture, i.e. ground moisture, from SAR measurements focusing on detailed in situ reference observations for several key geomaterials, i.e. sediments, typical in the study site. The mining site represents a limestone quarry located in the southeastern Finland. Our hypothesis is that sediment-specific well-calibrated models can be instrumental in improving soil moisture retrieval under different weather conditions to produce spatially explicit soil moisture estimates at high resolution compared to baseline approaches. Studied SAR data are represented by Copernicus Sentinel-1 C-band images, while auxiliary datasets include optical Sentinel-2 data. Reference data were collected using IoT enabled capacitance sensors. The reference data were calibrated based on laboratory analyses conducted on the different sediment types studied, including organic soil, clay, gravel, and flotation sand. The examined machine learning (ML) methods include XGBoost, LightGBM, random forest, support vector regression, linear regression and k-nearest neighbors. The performance of ML algorithms was evaluated using different cross-validation techniques including a five-fold approach as well as Leave-One-Sensor-Out (LOSO) to assess predictive accuracy and transferability to unseen sensors. The best performance under random five-fold cross-validation was achieved with the most comprehensive feature set which combines Sentinel-1 backscatter, time-series based soil moisture indices (SMI), Sentinel-2 optical, topographic, and temperature predictors. SHAP analysis revealed that SAR based features such as VH backscatter, traditional SMI derived from VV backscatter, and incidence angle were among the most important multi-source predictors. Adding sediment information improved Sentinel-1-only retrievals by more than 2 vol-%, but provided little additional benefit when richer multi-source feature sets were used. In the best sediment-area-level configurations, RMSE decreased to 0.037–0.050 m 3 m − 3 (3.7-5.0 vol. % points ), with R 2 values reaching 0.90. Accuracy varied by sediment texture, with the lowest errors for clay and organic soil and higher errors for flotation sand and gravel. However, LOSO validation demonstrated substantially weaker and site-dependent transferability: R 2 ranged from 0.45 to 0.67 for organic soil at a southern site and from 0.07 to 0.21 for organic soil at a northern site. Thus, high within-dataset predictive accuracy did not translate uniformly to unseen sensor locations, highlighting the need for broader spatially independent validation.

title: Process-informed deep learning for interpretable forested wetland mapping under dense canopy
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Canopy-obscured hydrologic signals and gradual wetland–upland transitions hinder the delineation of forested wetlands, particularly when heterogeneous Earth-observation evidence is fused as an unstructured feature stack. We developed a process-informed multi-stream convolutional neural network (CNN) for mapping forested wetlands on a 10-m modelling grid in the Changbai Mountains, China. The model used 85 covariates derived from Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, ALOS-2 PALSAR-2, and Copernicus DEM GLO-30. These covariates were assigned a priori to five predictor streams and processed by separate CNN branches before fusion. Relative to a capacity-matched single-stream baseline, the grouped architecture increased forested-wetland F1 by 3.42 percentage points across five validation folds, whereas the gain on the fixed held-out test set was smaller (+1.03 percentage points). For map production, the probability-averaged five-fold ensemble achieved an overall accuracy of 0.873, a macro-F1 of 0.882, and a forested-wetland F1 of 0.836 on the fixed held-out test set. To interpret correlated predictors, group-aggregated SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and k-nearest-neighbor conditional replacement were used to characterize global and conditional model reliance. Among correctly classified forested-wetland samples, global reliance was greatest for temporal features and phenology, whereas conditional replacement indicated the greatest residual model reliance for hydrology, followed by topography. Direct pixel counting yielded a map-derived forested-wetland area of 686.6 km 2 , concentrated mainly in peripheral plains and hills. This framework combines process-informed feature organization with dependence-aware interpretation to support interpretable regional mapping of canopy-obscured forested wetlands.

title: Generative Point Cloud Registration With Match-ControlNet
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel 3D registration paradigm, Generative Point Cloud Registration, which bridges advanced 2D generative models with 3D matching tasks to enhance registration performance. Our key idea is to generate cross-view consistent image pairs that are well-aligned with the source and target point clouds, enabling geometry-color feature fusion to facilitate robust matching. To ensure high-quality matching, the generated image pair should feature both 2D-3D geometric consistency and cross-view texture consistency. To this end, we introduce DepthMatch-ControlNet and LiDARMatch-ControlNet, two matching-specific, controllable 2D generative models. Specifically, for depth camera-based 3D registration with point clouds derived from the depth maps, DepthMatch-ControlNet leverages the depth-conditioned generation capabilities of ControlNet to synthesize perspective-view RGB images that are geometrically consistent with depth maps, ensuring accurate 2D-3D alignment. Additionally, by incorporating a coupled conditional denoising scheme and coupled prompt guidance, it further promotes cross-view feature interaction, guiding texture consistency generation. To address LiDAR-based 3D registration with point clouds captured by LiDAR sensors, LiDARMatch-ControlNet extends this framework by conditioning on paired equirectangular range maps projected from 360$^\circ$ LiDAR point clouds, generating corresponding panoramic RGB images. Our generative 3D registration paradigm is general and can be seamlessly integrated into a wide range of existing registration methods to improve their performance. Extensive experiments on the 3DMatch and ScanNet datasets (for depth-camera settings), as well as the Dur360BEV dataset (for LiDAR settings), demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

title: Image Quality Assessment for Machine-oriented Communication
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: The rapid development of Multimoal Large Language Models (MLLMs) has driven the evolution of communication paradigms, making the transmission of visual information in extremely low-bandwidth possible. However, as it is oriented toward computer vision tasks rather than humans, there is no widely accepted metric for its evaluation. To address this issue, we conduct a comprehensive visual quality assessment of machine oriented communication systems. Specifically, we (1) at the source level: a generative codec framework is established, with a MLLM communication pipeline through cross-modal generation between images and text. (2) at the channel level: images are transmitted using channel encoding/decoding strategies in different physical environments, and construct a dataset with 12k pairs of reference/distorted images. (3) at the sink level: 50 computer vision models are implemented to conduct 600k inferences on 5 downstream tasks, to characterize the differences between refer ence/distorted image pairs. (4) at the evaluation level: benchmark 18 cutting-edge Image Quality Assessment (IQA) methods, and develop a novel Mixture-of-Experts metric, termed CFA-MoE, to serve as a strong baseline for this task. Experimental results show that the current IQA algorithms cannot accurately evaluate machine-oriented distortions, highlighting the importance and challenge of this task. It is expected this dataset and baseline to facilitate future IQA algorithms and promote the communication paradigms from human to machine preference. Code will be available at: https://github.com/aiben-ch/MoQAD.

title: SpaRRTa: A Synthetic Benchmark for Evaluating Spatial Intelligence in Visual Foundation Models
abstract: Abstract Visual Foundation Models (VFMs), such as DINO and CLIP, excel in semantic understanding of images but exhibit limited spatial reasoning capabilities, which limits their applicability to embodied systems. As a result, recent work has incorporated some 3D tasks (such as depth estimation) into VFM training. However, VFM performance remains inconsistent across other spatial tasks, raising the question of whether these models truly possess spatial awareness or overfit to specific 3D objectives. To address this question, we introduce the Spatial Relation Recognition Task (SpaRRTa) benchmark, which evaluates the ability of VFMs to identify static directional relations between visible objects. Unlike traditional 3D objectives that focus on precise metric prediction (e.g., surface normal estimation), SpaRRTa probes a fundamental capability underpinning more advanced forms of human-like spatial understanding. SpaRRTa generates an arbitrary number of photorealistic images with diverse scenes and fully controllable object arrangements, along with freely accessible spatial annotations. Evaluating a range of state-of-the-art VFMs, we reveal significant disparities in their ability to encode directional spatial relations. Through our analysis, we provide insights into the mechanisms that support or hinder this form of spatial awareness in modern VFMs. We hope that SpaRRTa will serve as a useful tool for guiding the development of future spatially aware visual models. Our project page can be found at https://sparrta.gmum.net/ .

title: LEAD++: Unsupervised Fine-Grained Visual Representation Learning with Multi-context Enhanced Entropy-Based Adaptive Distillation
Block-Wise Variable Conditional Diffusion for High-Fidelity Text-to-4D Generation
abstract: Abstract Text-to-4D scene generation is currently impeded by three primary challenges: the prohibitive memory cost of training high-dimensional diffusion models, the semantic misalignment arising from the failure to disentangle static object identity from dynamic motion in text conditioning, and the scarcity of high-quality datasets that accurately correlate subjects, motions, and environments. To surmount these challenges, we present Swin4D , an end-to-end framework for efficient and high-fidelity text-to-4D synthesis. First, we introduce a Block-wise Variable Conditional Diffusion strategy, which mitigates memory constraints and prevents overfitting by dynamically reconfiguring spatial dependencies during training. Second, we propose Global–Local Alignment , a hierarchical guidance mechanism that explicitly disentangles global scene context from local subject-action semantics via separate T5 and CLIP encoders, ensuring spatiotemporal consistency and fine-grained semantic fidelity regardless of prompt length. Finally, we address data limitations by curating RealSynth4D , a large-scale hybrid dataset combining 108k real-world captures with 72k AI-synthesised scenes, establishing robust correlations between subjects, actions, and complex backgrounds to significantly enhance model generalisation.
