RAVEN-Bench: A Paired EO-IR Video QA Benchmark for Aerial Multimodal Understanding
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have advanced rapidly in image and video understanding, yet their ability to reason over paired aerial electro-optical and infrared (EO-IR) videos remains poorly understood. Such video poses a harder test than standard RGB video QA: targets are often small, evidence may appear only briefly, viewpoints change with the platform, and useful cues may appear in only one stream. We introduce RAVEN-Bench (Reasoning over Aerial Videos with EO-IR aligNment), a paired EO-IR video QA benchmark for low-altitude aerial multimodal understanding. RAVEN-Bench contains 100 temporally aligned EO-IR video pairs and 1,200 human-authored four-way multiple-choice questions, each independently audited for answer keys, modality requirements, evidence intervals, and group validity. It supports EO-only, IR-only, and paired EO+IR evaluation, and uses hierarchical capability levels and structured question groups to diagnose paired-input gain beyond the stronger unimodal condition, unimodal reliance, target consistency, and evidence-chain coherence. We evaluate frontier, open-weight, and remote-sensing MLLMs, showing that aggregate accuracy can overstate evidence-supported EO-IR reasoning. RAVEN-Bench provides controlled modality conditions and group-level diagnostics for auditing whether progress on RGB video benchmarks transfers to aerial cross-spectral understanding. Code and data are available at https://github.com/yuhu990424/RAVEN-Bench and https://huggingface.co/datasets/TerraSenseAnalytics/RAVEN-Bench.

title: Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Multi-Dimensional Slope Change Problem
abstract: Slope change detection seeks to identify changes in the trends of time-ordered signals. We study the problem of fitting a multidimensional time series by continuous piecewise-linear functions with a shared continuous breakpoint and unrestricted slopes. We consider both the dense setting, in which every dimension may change slope, and the sparse setting, in which at most $k$ dimensions may change slope. Although the resulting optimization problems are nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear programs and may have irrational optimal solutions even for rational data, we prove that all six variants, corresponding to the $\ell_1$, $\ell_2$, and $\ell_\infty$ losses in both settings, are exactly solvable in polynomial time. For least-squares loss, we obtain efficient algorithms requiring $O(JT)$ operations in the dense setting and $O(J^2T\log J)$ operations in the sparse setting, where $T$ is the number of time points and $J$ is the number of dimensions. We implement these least-squares algorithms and evaluate them on simulated data and three real-world time series, namely, surface temperatures (ERA5), hand-tracking data from a mixed-reality headset (HoloAssist), and turbofan engine sensor data (NASA C-MAPSS). The dense algorithm solves instances with up to $J=10^5$ and $T=100$, that is, $10^7$ observations, in less than $0.1$ seconds on a laptop, while the sparse algorithm solves instances with about $10^3$ dimensions and up to $T=240$ in under a second. Compared with a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) formulation solved by Gurobi, our algorithms are several orders of magnitude faster (approximately $8.9 \times 10^3$ to $3.4 \times 10^6$ times) on instances where Gurobi terminates within its default optimality tolerance of $0.01\%$ optimality gap. On larger instances, Gurobi frequently reaches a 10,000-second time limit with substantial optimality gaps.

title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
abstract: Detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) objects is essential for ensuring the reliability and safety of object detectors in real-world deployment. We treat the decision on a detected box as a hypothesis test with the null hypothesis that the box covers an object of an in-distribution (ID) class. The null distribution changes with the size of the box and its contact with the image border, and the detector observes both. The test can therefore rank a box only against ID boxes of the same size and border contact, which gives a distribution-free bound on the false-alarm rate for each of them and uncovers the separation that one null distribution hides. The power of the test also rests on the layer it reads. Layers built only for the ID classes have no reason to keep what sets an unknown object apart, so the test reads the features before them. We propose \textbf{PLUM}, a training-free score that pools the last backbone stage inside the box and ranks its distance to the ID classes among ID boxes of the same size and border contact. On the standard benchmark, PLUM reaches the highest AUROC among the compared methods without external models, with 91.5 and 94.5 on PASCAL-VOC and 95.1 and 97.5 on BDD100K. Code: https://github.com/DDOZMI/PLUM

title: Enhanced Hyperspectral Nano-FTIR Imaging by Neural-Network-Based Processing of Multiple Signal Harmonics
abstract: Nano-FTIR spectroscopy combines infrared spectroscopy with nanometer-scale spatial resolution and enables hyperspectral nanoimaging. However, quantitative measurements typically rely on higher-harmonic near-field signals, which are largely background-free but suffer from low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Lower harmonics provide substantially higher SNR but contain significant background contributions that distort the near-field response and hinder quantitative analysis. Here, we introduce a cross-harmonic neural network (CHNN) that exploits the complementary information encoded in multiple harmonic channels to denoise third-harmonic hyperspectral data. Trained directly on experimental nano-FTIR datasets, the CHNN uses first- and second-harmonic spectra to improve the SNR of the third-harmonic response. Applied to a PMMA/PS polymer blend, it substantially reduces noise while preserving spectral features and nanoscale spatial contrast. Compared with conventional single-harmonic denoising using an autoencoder, the CHNN achieves superior noise suppression. These results demonstrate the potential of lower-harmonic signals for improving hyperspectral nano-FTIR imaging without increasing acquisition time.

title: MaskSCD: Bitemporal Mask Classification for Semantic Change Detection in Remote Sensing Images
abstract: Semantic change detection (SCD) identifies where the land surface has changed and which land-cover transition has taken place. Most deep SCD networks predict the change map and the land-cover map of each date with separate per-pixel decoders. These outputs need not agree, so a pixel can be labeled as changed although it has the same class at both dates, and per-pixel decisions fragment objects. We present MaskSCD, which formulates SCD as the mask classification of a bitemporal label-pair image. Each bitemporal segment, a region of constant land-cover class pair, is predicted as one mask shared by both dates together with one class per date, and the change map is derived from the predicted class pair. This formulation keeps the change and semantic maps consistent and the label space linear in the number of classes. A bitemporal masked-attention transformer decoder implements it by reading each segment in both images and relating the two readings, and a bitemporal fusion pyramid provides per-date and change-aware features. MaskSCD is evaluated on SECOND, Landsat-SCD and Hi-UCD, which span 0.1 to 30 m resolution and four to nine land-cover classes, against fourteen recent SCD models re-trained under one protocol. MaskSCD achieves the best separated kappa, semantic change $F_1$ and transition $F_1$ on all three datasets and exceeds the strongest competitor by about five points in mean separated kappa. It produces no contradictory change pixels, which account for nearly 30% of the predicted change of some multi-task networks. The code is available at https://github.com/EricYu97/MaskSCD.

title: Unlocking Cross-Attention in Label-Scarce Regimes: A Weakly Supervised Approach for Video Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Weakly Supervised Video Semantic Segmentation (WS-VSS) aims to learn temporally consistent semantic object masks in videos using only video-level labels. While fully supervised models successfully learn temporal relationships by means of cross-attention, training these temporal weights under weak supervision is unstable and even pushes the model below its single-frame baseline. Therefore, existing WS-VSS methods exploit temporal consistency by relying on external priors, such as optical flow. Unfortunately these cues are non-semantic, computationally expensive and noisy, degrading the supervisory signal. Instead of supervising attention weights directly or using external priors, we propose MemCAM, a WS-VSS transformer framework that learns temporal cross-attention directly through feature-space self-supervision. MemCAM introduces a CAM Propagation Algorithm that synthesizes a supervisory signal by propagating past CAMs according to patch-level feature similarities in the latent space. Specifically, we constrain their induced CAMs through a consistency objective between predicted and propagated maps, stabilizing temporal attention learning. Experiments on the YouTube-Objects v2.2 and WS$^2$ datasets demonstrate that MemCAM consistently outperforms the temporal localization and segmentation performance of WS-VSS alternatives, showing that cross-attention can be effectively trained in label-scarce video settings through internal self-supervision.

title: Lens: Training-Free Semantic Search for Cross-Tile Object and Scene Retrieval in Satellite Imagery
abstract: We developed Lens, a training-free system for semantic object and scene search across large satellite mosaics that requires no detector trained for the class of interest. Lens represents each tile with a frozen, self-supervised vision transformer (DINOv3), removes the positional bias in its dense features by projecting them onto the subspace orthogonal to a positional basis estimated once from a constant image, and centers the debiased features on the mean feature computed across the whole area before comparison. Lens forms a query by averaging the centered features of a small neighborhood of patches around a chosen point, or of an entire tile for scene-level search, and matches it against the index by cosine similarity. It stores the centered patch features in a byte-quantized similarity index that supports real-time range search over a mosaic of thousands of patches, and a coarser whole-tile embedding index for scene-level retrieval. A guided upsampling network (AnyUp) runs once per tile to recover pixel-accurate boundaries beyond the native feature grid, and the result is cached so later queries reuse it. We evaluated Lens on the 5,128-tile DFC2020 test set and ran it as an interactive tool on five Sentinel-2 areas spanning agricultural, industrial, and desert terrain; the pipeline is not tied to a specific sensor. On DFC2020 a single click reaches 0.09 to 0.80 pixel F1 across eight land-cover classes at the per-class best threshold, with a mean F1 of 0.39, and it beats a pairwise INSID3 baseline on six of the eight classes at roughly four hundred times lower query cost. Indexing 1.31 million patches takes 169 s on one CPU thread, and a click returns a rendered overlay in 6 to 10 ms.

title: SWAM: Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging for Efficient Vision Transformers
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) achieve strong performance on image recognition tasks, yet their quadratic self-attention complexity over input tokens creates prohibitive computational costs for practical deployment. Token reduction methods offer a practical solution by progressively reducing the token sequence during the forward pass. We propose Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging (SWAM), a training-based token merging framework that extends the Bipartite Soft Matching (BSM) with two saliency-aware mechanisms. We introduce a two-step matching formulation in which cosine similarity decides candidate pairs, while a multiplicative maximum saliency penalty regulates their selection for merging. We then further use asymmetric exponential saliency-weighted aggregation, which allows more salient tokens to contribute more strongly to the merged representation. A lightweight MLP-based saliency prediction module (75k parameters per stage, 1% of backbone parameters) supervised via attention rollout is trained end-to-end jointly with a DeiT-Small backbone using a composite cross-entropy, knowledge-distillation, and saliency-alignment objective. On CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet-100, under a conservative schedule that reduces tokens from 196 to 100 patch tokens, with the CLS token retained throughout, 27.5% FLOPs reduction and 1.35 times speedup, SWAM matches or exceeds baseline across the reported results. Under an aggressive schedule (196 to 70 tokens with the CLS token kept throughout, 33.8% FLOPs reduction, and 1.46 times speedup), accuracy gains are achieved on ImageNet-100 (+0.23%) with minimal losses on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet.

title: Few-Shot Open-Set Hyperspectral Pixel-Wise Classification with Spatial Aware Label Propagation
abstract: Pixelwise classification of hyperspectral images (HSI) is a fundamental task in remote sensing, but its deployment in real-world applications is often limited by the scarcity of labeled data and the presence of unknown classes at inference time. In this work, we propose Few-shot Open-set hyperspectral recognition from Self-Supervised Learning training (FOSSeL), a unified framework for few-shot, open-set hyperspectral pixelwise classification that does not require supervised training. The proposed approach first leverages self-supervised learning to construct a discriminative feature space from unlabeled data. Then, given a small set of labeled seed pixels, class predictions are obtained through spatially-aware graph-based label propagation over superpixel representations, enabling the joint exploitation of spectral similarity and spatial consistency. To address the open-set scenario, we introduce simple yet effective strategies to identify pixels that do not belong to the known classes. We evaluate FOSSeL on three benchmark hyperspectral datasets under multiple few-shot settings. The results show that the proposed framework achieves competitive or superior performance compared to fully supervised methods while maintaining robustness in the presence of unknown classes. These findings highlight the potential of combining self-supervised feature learning with graph-based inference for practical HSI analysis in low-annotation and open-world scenarios.

title: From Images to Grounded Edits: A Real-World Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction in Handwritten Essays
abstract: Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (CGEC) is typically formulated as a text-to-text problem. While suitable for digital texts, this formulation falls short in real-world K-12 education, where AI-assisted corrections are expected directly on essay images, which are primarily handwritten and exhibit many irregularities. To bridge this gap, we introduce Grounded Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (G-CGEC), an image-to-grounded-edit task requiring systems to predict both corrections and their positions on essay images. We propose G-CGEC-Eval, a benchmark comprising real-world images of K-12 Chinese essays with fine-grained annotations. For evaluation, we adapt IoU-based metrics from object detection and propose a more tolerant alternative based on center-distance matching. Using this benchmark, we evaluate open-source and proprietary vision-language models under a direct single-pass setting, as well as settings with auxiliary components (OCR and character grounding) coordinated via pipelining or agentic harnessing. Results show that even top-tier proprietary models perform surprisingly poorly in the single-pass setting, while pipelining and agentic harnessing yield meaningful improvements. Notably, an error-type-based multi-agent workflow achieves the best performance, establishing it as the strongest baseline for future G-CGEC research. Through ablations and fine-grained analysis, we find the task remains far from solved, with linguistic error discovery and character-level grounding as the primary bottlenecks. This underscores the need for models that better integrate visual perception with linguistic reasoning and visual grounding.

title: nnAEU: a Simple and Efficient CNN-Autoencoder for Hyperspectral Unmixing
abstract: Deep learning-based hyperspectral unmixing (HSU) has followed a trajectory of increasing architectural complexity, from simple autoencoders to transformers and, most recently, Mamba-based models, each claiming to advance the state of the art. Contrary to this trend, we propose a lightweight CNN-based autoencoder, coined "Not New Autoencoder Unmixing" (nnAEU). It is derived from the backbone of UNMamba (2025) through a pruning study that removes the Mamba component entirely. nnAEU uses less than 10 times fewer parameters than UNMamba, and far fewer than other transformer- and GAN-based methods, while outperforming them in accuracy. We provide a complete, minimal, reproducible code, available at https://gitlab.telecom-paris.fr/ring/nnAEU.git.

title: See and Detect: Image-Driven Open-Vocabulary Multi-View 3D Object Detection
abstract: Recent open-vocabulary multi-view indoor 3D detection methods typically follow a point-cloud-driven pipeline, where pseudo 3D boxes are generated from reconstructed or estimated geometry and semantic labels are inferred from projected regions. However, such a design makes box generation dependent on the completeness of point clouds and restricts semantic learning to local appearance, causing inferior 3D object localization and open-vocabulary classification. In this paper, we present See and Detect, an image-driven framework that uses multi-view images as the primary evidence for 3D box and semantic label generation. For box generation, we first discover object candidates from individual images, enabling objects missing in point clouds to be recovered from visual evidence. However, single-view predictions are often noisy and redundant. To address this, we propose multi-view consensus box consolidation to fuse spatially consistent predictions across views, and box quality assessment to reduce the impact of boxes with partial object coverage. For semantic label generation, we introduce context-aware semantic learning, where semantic labels are queried from full image context, enabling more accurate semantic prediction. Extensive experiments on ScanNet and ARKitScenes demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art open-vocabulary multi-view 3D detection performance while running over 500$\times$ faster than the previous state-of-the-art method.

title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). AstroVink-TREX: Automated strong gravitational lens segmentation as input for mass modelling pipelines
abstract: Strong gravitational lens modelling requires the lens light, lensed source light, and contaminants to be separated in each image before mass modelling codes can fit the system. Within Euclid this separation has so far been done by hand, which does not scale to the more than 15,000 candidates in the Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) catalogue of Data Release 1 (DR1). We present AstroVink-TREX , a neural network that performs this separation automatically and predicts three flux maps, in a standard format directly usable by mass-modelling pipelines. The network uses a hybrid architecture, pairing a vision transformer encoder reused from the lens detection network with a parallel convolutional branch. A custom loss function penalises both flux and structural error, while allowing independent weighting per component. From the network's predictions we also derive the modelling centre, fitting region, conjugate points, and binary maps, providing all the inputs that a modelling pipeline needs to run without manual setup. We evaluate the efficiency of the network on DR1 systems against existing fits and through expert validation. Across approximately 3000 inspected systems, taking 75% agreement between inspectors, just 39 lens models fail because of a segmentation error. Following this validation, the network provides the component separation and modelling setup for every system modelled in DR1. With automated segmentation, lens modelling is no longer limited by manual preprocessing and can now operate at the same scale as lens discovery.

title: Can Large Language Models Optimize Pretrained Neural Network Weights? A Multi-Phase Empirical Evaluation of Gradient-Free Editing in YOLO26 Object Detection
abstract: Direct weight editing offers a gradient-free alternative to fine-tuning pretrained detectors, but its generalization and the value of large language model (LLM) guidance remain uncertain. We evaluate five experimental phases using YOLO26 models and MS COCO, comparing deterministic scaling, random perturbations, differential evolution, CMA-ES, structured interventions, real local-LLM proposals, failure-aware guidance, and hybrid LLM-CMA-ES against a matched random-policy control. Optimization uses native Ultralytics mAP50-95 on 1,000 COCO Val2017 images; selected candidates are assessed on a disjoint, previously examined 1,500-image subset, with COCO API AP50-95 reported separately where available. Increasing the CMA-ES budget from 8 to 250 evaluations raised development gains from +0.11 to +0.28 percentage points, while selection changes remained negative (-0.03 to -0.12 points); the 250-evaluation result uses one seed. The hybrid LLM approach showed no statistically established advantage over random-policy guidance (p = 0.612, 0.369, and 0.694 at budgets 8, 25, and 50). Five-seed YOLO26m replication yielded a COCO API AP difference of +0.004 points (95% CI: -0.026 to +0.034). Of 225 archived LLM proposals, 53 satisfy the final strict schema; early tensor-level execution cannot be fully verified. Genuine LLM-mediated weight editing is feasible, but the tested approaches did not demonstrate consistent transfer beyond the development subset or a measurable LLM advantage.

title: A novel approach for soil moisture retrieval via fusing multi-spaceborne GNSS-R observations in entire Tibetan Plateau
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Spaceborne GNSS-Reflectometry (GNSS-R) is a powerful technology for soil moisture (SM) retrieval. However, complex topography and steep slopes over the Tibetan Plateau lead to significant signal loss and sampling sparsity. This study proposes a novel Dirichlet-prior-guided Vision Transformer (DG-ViT) framework to fuse multi-source observations from CYGNSS, Tianmu-1, and the FY-3E/F/G constellation. The novel DG-ViT framework incorporates land cover informed prior guidance into multi-spaceborne surface reflectivity (SR) fusion, and its performance is evaluated against single-source retrievals and traditional machine learning algorithms. To assess generalization, the fused SR was coupled with six mainstream machine learning algorithms (RF, XGBoost, ANN, BP, SVM, and GBDT) for 9 km daily SM retrieval, with multi-scale validation conducted against ERA5 SM and nine in-situ stations. Results demonstrate that the DG-ViT framework achieves a daily SR coverage of 89.49 %, representing an improvement of 20.13 % and 14.32 % over standalone CYGNSS and Tianmu-1 data, respectively. In addition, this fusion strategy overcomes the coverage gap of CYGNSS north of 38°N and compensates for the inability of individual FY-3 missions to support daily SM retrieval. In comparative assessments, the DG-ViT combined with RF yields superior performance (R = 0.955, RMSE = 0.039 cm 3 /cm 3 , bias = 0.000 cm 3 /cm 3 ), markedly enhancing retrieval accuracy relative to results derived from single-source CYGNSS or Tianmu-1 SR. In-situ validation shows ubRMSE values between 0.0232 and 0.0619 cm 3 /cm 3 , a 15.1 % precision gain over ERA5 SM. The proposed DG-ViT combined with RF approach effectively exploits the complementarity among multi-spaceborne GNSS-R observations over the entire Tibetan Plateau, thereby compensating for the signal deficiencies of individual missions. This fusion approach provides a novel perspective for SM retrieval in high-altitude areas, specifically improving daily SR coverage and SM retrieval accuracy through fusion of multi-spaceborne GNSS-R observations with land cover informed prior guidance.

title: ObsGate-SST: observation-gated background–detail learning for global daily sea surface temperature reconstruction
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Infrared cloud screening and incomplete sampling limit the process-scale use of daily satellite sea surface temperature (SST), whereas many gap-filled Level-4 analyses attenuate narrow fronts, tropical-cyclone cold wakes and short-lived warm extremes. This study presents ObsGate-SST, an observation-gated background–detail learning framework for global daily SST reconstruction. The model ingests cloud-contaminated ODYSSEA L3S SST, a valid-pixel mask and an OISST v2.1 prior. A low-frequency branch estimates the basin-scale thermal background, a high-frequency branch reconstructs gradient and texture residuals from observed pixels, and a deterministic observation gate copies all valid satellite observations exactly so that inference is restricted to missing open-ocean pixels. Training used 2000–2020 daily fields, validation used 2021–2022 and independent testing used 2023–2025. Against 2023 quality-level-5 iQuam matchups, monthly bias ranged from 0.193 to 0.291 °C, RMSE from 0.637 to 0.849 °C and correlation from 0.993 to 0.996 across 902,665 collocations. A cloud-gap-shaped withheld-observed-pixel audit isolated inferred-pixel skill: ObsGate-SST achieved the lowest pooled RMSE (0.4802 °C), while removing the low-frequency branch, high-frequency branch, gradient/detail loss and physical/prior regularization increased RMSE by 17.0 %, 9.9 %, 3.9 % and 2.0 %, respectively. Relative to DINEOF, U-Net, Swin-Unet and SegNet under common masks, ObsGate-SST better retained spectral energy, frontal continuity, marine-heatwave structure, typhoon cold wakes and equatorial Pacific gradients. These results support observation-gated multiscale learning as a physically interpretable strategy for reconstructing incomplete satellite SST without sacrificing observed-pixel fidelity.

title: Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 responses to Hansen-reported forest loss in the Peruvian Amazon: Timing and spatial sensitivity
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Satellite signals preceding recorded tropical forest loss are rarely tested against locations without loss. We compared the timing of Sentinel-1 co-polarised (VV) and cross-polarised (VH) backscatter and three Sentinel-2 indices (Normalized Burn Ratio, NBR; Normalized Difference Moisture Index, NDMI; Normalized Difference Red Edge index, NDRE) with Hansen Global Forest Change loss years in the Ucayali Region of the Peruvian Amazon (2019–2025). Hansen loss years served as an annual, satellite-derived reference rather than independent ground truth. Monthly time series at 819 locations with Hansen loss in 2021–2024 at the central 30 m pixel were compared with 2,588 non-loss locations using before-after analysis, superposed epoch analysis and single-change-point breakpoint detection with a pseudo-year null model. Sensitivity to spatial matching was tested with 50–250 m buffers, and canopy height from the Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation was examined exploratorily. All variables declined around the Hansen loss year relative to non-loss locations, most strongly for Sentinel-2 (Cliff’s δ = − 0.66 to − 0.76; Sentinel-1: −0.27 to − 0.30). Negative breakpoints occurred at 74–82% of loss locations for the Sentinel-2 indices, mostly in the loss year. Breakpoints preceding the loss year occurred at 9.5–19.0% of loss locations, exceeding the non-loss comparison only for NBR (+4.9 percentage points) and NDRE (+3.8) at the primary penalty. Apparent pre-loss rates increased with buffer size and depended on breakpoint selection, and exploratory GEDI analysis found no detectable association between canopy height and breakpoint timing. Pre-loss satellite signals should be tested against non-loss baselines before being interpreted as early warning.

title: Integrating vegetation phenology and SWOT-derived surface water dynamics for improved county-scale winter wheat yield prediction
abstract: Winter wheat yield is shaped by crop growth status and surface hydrological conditions. However, remote-sensing approaches based primarily on vegetation index (VI) time series may not fully represent the surrounding surface-water environment in county-scale yield prediction. We integrated growth-stage VI features with surface-water dynamics derived from the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission to predict county-level winter wheat yield in Henan Province, China. We evaluated direct feature fusion, same-year residual correction, and target-year residual correction following cross-year VI extrapolation using outer ten-fold cross-validation. Inner five-fold cross-fitting generated same-year VI residual targets exclusively within each outer training set. The VI-only model achieved R2 = 0.772, RMSE = 0.688 t ha−1, and MAE = 0.510 t ha−1. Direct incorporation of SWOT features reduced predictive accuracy, with R2 = 0.749, RMSE = 0.721 t ha−1, and MAE = 0.547 t ha−1. By contrast, SWOT-based residual correction yielded a clearer improvement in same-year prediction, increasing R2 to 0.795 and reducing RMSE to 0.652 t ha−1. The historical VI model was trained on 2010–2021, independently tested on 2022–2023, and extrapolated to 2024, where it achieved R2 = 0.676, RMSE = 0.819 t ha−1, and MAE = 0.611 t ha−1. Calibrated using observed 2024 yields from training counties and evaluated on held-out 2024 counties, subsequent target-year residual correction with concurrent SWOT features increased R2 to 0.749 and reduced RMSE and MAE to 0.722 and 0.524 t ha−1, respectively. SHAP analysis showed that SWOT contributions were concentrated during seeding, emergence, overwintering, green, heading–flowering, and filling and varied by spatial scale and prediction scenario. Overall, SWOT-derived surface-water observations provided complementary predictive information relative to the evaluated VI baselines, particularly for target-year spatial calibration. Their broader applicability across regions, crops, and years remains to be established through independent validation.

title: Person Recognition at Altitude and Range: Fusion of Face, Body Shape and Gait
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: We address the problem of whole-body person recognition in unconstrained environments. This problem arises in surveillance scenarios such as those in the IARPA Biometric Recognition and Identification at Altitude and Range (BRIAR) program, where biometric data is captured at long standoff distances, elevated viewing angles, and under adverse atmospheric conditions (e.g., turbulence and high wind velocity). To this end, we propose FarSight, a unified end-to-end system for person recognition that integrates complementary biometric cues across face, gait, and body shape modalities. FarSight comprises four core modules: multi-subject detection and tracking, recognition-aware video restoration, modality-specific biometric feature encoding, and quality-guided multi-modal fusion. Rather than treating these modules as independent processing stages, FarSight coordinates key stage-level decisions around the final biometric objective: tracking maintains identity-consistent temporal evidence, restoration is selectively invoked and optimized for recognition, and modality-quality estimates guide score fusion. This coordinated design supports recognition under degraded image conditions, large pose and scale variations, and cross-domain gaps. Extensive experiments on the BRIAR dataset, one of the most comprehensive benchmarks for long-range, multi-modal biometric recognition, demonstrate the effectiveness of FarSight. Compared with our preliminary system [1] on the Face-Included treatment set of BRIAR EVP 5.0.1, the current system improves 1:1 verification (TAR@0.1% FAR) by 34.4 percentage points and closed-set identification (Rank-20) by 17.8 percentage points, while reducing open-set identification errors (FNIR@1% FPIR) by 34.3 percentage points. Furthermore, FarSight was evaluated in the 2025 NIST RTE Face in Video Evaluation (FIVE), which conducts standardized face recognition testing on the BRIAR dataset. These results establish FarSight as a state-of-the-art solution for operational biometric recognition in challenging real-world conditions.

title: Representation of Directed Acyclic Graphs by Sequences of Instructions for Symbolic Regression
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Symbolic Regression (SR) aims to discover a closed-form mathematical expression that fits an observed dataset by representing those expressions as Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs). A DAG with k internal nodes admits Θ(k!) equivalent node orderings of the same expression, so structurally identical candidates repeatedly reach the fitness evaluator of the solver model, consuming search budget. We introduce ISALSR (Instruction Set and Language for Symbolic Regression), an encoding that maps every labeled DAG to a canonical string over a two-tier alphabet of structural and operation-labeled tokens. Canonical strings are reached via a greedy algorithm guided by 1-Weisfeiler-Leman (1-WL) subtree hashing. We prove that the canonical string is a complete labeled-DAG invariant under a reachability condition: two expressions share their string if and only if their DAGs are isomorphic. ISALSR integrates at the evaluation boundary and needs no change to the host search algorithm. It has been validated on a systematic enumerator (UDFS) and an evolutionary search (Bingo) over a 70-problem suite assembled from nine published benchmarks, against both the host solvers' native representation and a naive hash of a fixed-order DAG serialization. Canonicalization eliminates a mean of 38.1% of evaluations on UDFS and 43.7% on Bingo, on every one of the 70 problems under both hosts. A paired test across problems puts its reduction factor above that of the naive hash at a Cohen's d of 2.54 and 7.05, both at p < 10-12. Canonicalization consumes 0.04% of run time on UDFS and 16.1% on Bingo. Deduplication is therefore close to free where a fitness evaluation costs orders of magnitude more than a canonical string, and expensive where the two are comparable. ISALSR is the first instruction-based graph encoding to carry operation labels, edge direction and a non-commutative operator, and because the canonical form is itself a string, it also gives sequence models a target that is invariant to node renumbering. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/MarioPasc/IsalSR.

title: A Simple but Efficient Method to Achieve High Performance with Extreme Sparsity
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Pruning effectively removes redundant parameters and computations from neural networks, reduces model storage space, and saves time, memory, and energy during the training and inference phases. However, current pruning methods perform well at moderate and high sparsity, but the performance difference with dense network models at extreme sparsity is huge. In order to bridge the accuracy gap between extremely sparse and dense models, this paper proposes a simple but efficient pruning strategy-Tensor Decomposition Based Iterative Magnitude Pruning (TDIMP) method. This strategy uses tensor theory to optimize the model structure before IMP to reduce the search space of the sparse subnetwork during pruning, thus improving the hit rate of the optimal sparse subnetwork. Specifically, firstly, the weight matrix or weight tensor of the dense model is represented as a low-rank tensor decomposition format, and the feature extraction capability of the base module is enhanced by multi-step chaining operations to construct a low-rank compact network model. Secondly, IMP is performed on the low-rank model. The weight updates are sampled multiple times at the later stages of model training during each magnitude pruning process to smooth the oscillations of the learning trajectory and improve the performance of the sparse model. To evaluate the superiority of TDIMP, we first conducted extensive experiments using LSTM, VGGNet, ResNet, and Transformer architectures on UCF11, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet datasets at sparsities ranging from 98% to 99.9%, and compared it with state-of-the-art methods. Experimental results show that TDIMP has higher accuracy, faster inference and less storage space than the pruning at initialization, dynamic sparse training, and iterative pruning methods in the extreme sparse case. In addition, TDIMP also has faster training speed than IMP methods.

title: 2D Gaussian Splatting for Semantic Segmentation via Discrete-to-Continuous Representation toward Boundary-Preserving Feature Upsampling
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: High-quality semantic segmentation requires not only rich semantic understanding but also precise delineation of object boundaries. While prevailing methods rely on discrete feature representations that often lead to boundary misalignment, jagged contours, and blurry edges along complex contours, we present GSSeg, a novel semantic segmentation paradigm based on Gaussian Splatting that has been successfully applied to 3D scene reconstruction. Specifically, GSSeg reformulates the discrete feature space as continuous Gaussian fields, thereby rendering spatial continuity modeling to produce high-quality segmentation results. However, directly adapting 2DGS to existing pipelines suffers from the structural granularity loss in low-resolution features and the inherent low-pass limitations of Gaussian rendering. To address the insufficient structural granularity available for discrete-to-continuous transformation, we propose the cross-layer neighborhood interaction scheme utilizing alternating global scanning, which establishes cross-scale contextual cues to enhance adaptive Gaussian kernel generation. Additionally, addressing the inherent low-pass limitations of Gaussian rendering, we introduce spatial uncertainty-aware resampling driven by resolution bias estimation, which selectively compensates for high-frequency details attenuated during Gaussian rendering. Furthermore, we introduce an effective Gaussian kernel initialization strategy that approximates Gaussian radial basis function interpolation, ensuring model training stability. Comprehensive experiments on standard benchmarks, especially high-resolution matting-level dataset MaSS13K, demonstrate that GSSeg achieves state-of-the-art performance.

title: Seeing Text Clearly in the Dark: Unifying Localization and Enhancement via Deep Morphological Synergy
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Low-light text localization, an interdisciplinary field, has gained significant attention recently. The goal is to provide enhanced text locational information beneficial for both machine and human vision. Existing one-stage and two-stage methods either rely on single detectors specially designed for low-light conditions or on a simple cascade of detectors and enhancers, both of which exhibit limitations in effectively addressing the joint task of enhancement and text localization simultaneously. Relying solely on a single set of dual operations in deep morphology, we link the joint task via a bidirectional morphological sync bridge that ensures the simultaneous flow of two directions: one preserving the topological connectivity of text and the other improving its exposure level under low-light conditions. We then introduce a novel bi-level synergistic learning strategy, where text localization serves as the upper-level task and enhancement as the lower-level task. This strategy leverages bidirectional connectivity in the deep morphological sync bridge as a learnable constraint and alternately updates coupled gradients with different update frequencies to optimize the joint task. Extensive experiments on the low-light text localization dataset LATeD demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in both tasks. The code will be released.

title: Kernel Adaptive Deformable Convolution for Remote Sensing Object Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Modeling geometric variations, particularly the extreme fluctuations in scale and shape, stands as a persistent challenge in computer vision, which is significantly exacerbated in remote sensing object detection (RSOD). Existing methods are often constrained by the fixed geometric topology of standard convolutions or the insufficient representation power of linear feature aggregation, making it difficult to strike an ideal balance between adaptability and computational efficiency. To address these challenges, we propose a novel scale- and shape-adaptive method named Kernel Adaptive Deformable Convolution (KAD-Conv). Specifically, KAD-Conv employs a specialized Deformable Spatial Convolution (DSC) at its core to adaptively adjust sampling locations, while reformulating the mask generation process to fully leverage the mask's potential for discriminative feature modulation. In KAD-Conv, we further introduce a Scale-aware Kernel Adaptive mechanism, which enables the dynamic adjustment of sampling scales to effectively capture object representations across extreme scale variations without increasing kernel size. With KAD-Conv, we develop a novel object detection network based on Multi-task Guided Learning (MGL), called KAD-CNet. Extensive experiments conducted on widely used remote sensing benchmark datasets, including DOTA-v1.0, DIOR, and NWPU VHR-10, along with validation on natural scenes exhibiting extreme geometric variations, have validated the effectiveness of the proposed KAD-CNet. Moreover, comprehensive comparisons against various YOLO-series models further underscore the practical value and efficiency of the proposed approach.

title: GenHOI: Generalizing Text-driven 4D Human-Object Interaction Synthesis for Unseen Objects
HENet++: Hybrid Encoding and Multi-task Learning for 3D Perception and Planning in Autonomous Driving
Dynamic Knowledge-Aware for Streaming View Clustering
abstract: In real scenarios, multi-view data are often continuously acquired in the form of view streams, giving rise to the task of Streaming View Clustering (SVC). However, most existing methods rely on view-specific knowledge to guide the learning of the current view, while neglecting the shared, view-invariant knowledge structure across views. As a result, the model progressively forgets the commonalities between current and historical views during training, i.e., catastrophic forgetting, which leads to severe fluctuations in clustering performance under different input sequences. To address this issue, we propose a Dynamic kNowledge-Aware (DNA) framework for SVC, which is designed to mitigate the negative impact of catastrophic forgetting effectively. The proposed DNA framework consists of two main stages: the initial learning stage and the continual learning stage. Specifically, during the initial learning stage, we employ knowledge-aware learning to extract prototype knowledge from the first acquired view and construct an initial knowledge base. During the continual learning stage, we leverage knowledge aggregation learning to maximize the consistency between the prototype knowledge of the current view and the historical knowledge, and then fuse them into a new prototype knowledge and update the knowledge base, thereby ensuring the completeness of the learned knowledge. Finally, through structural guidance learning, the updated knowledge base is used to steer the sample distribution of the current view, thereby ensuring distributional consistency across different views. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that DNA consistently and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at https://github.com/hl-yuan/DNA.

title: Degradation-aware Infrared Image Super-Resolution
abstract: Infrared image super-resolution (IISR) is inherently more challenging than its visible-light counterpart due to the presence of structured, infrared-specific degradations, including thermal noise, fixed-pattern noise, and spatially non-uniform blur. These degradations deviate substantially from commonly assumed degradation models and often lead existing methods to produce unstable structures, amplified noise, or hallucinated textures. In this work, we present DIRSR, a degradation-aware framework for infrared image super-resolution that explicitly incorporates infrared degradation perception into the restoration process. The proposed approach characterizes instance-level infrared degradation conditions and leverages degradation-aware semantic guidance to regulate the trade-off between perceptual quality and structural fidelity. In addition, infrared imaging priors are embedded into a physics-informed, region-aware optimization objective to enhance foreground structural consistency while suppressing spurious background details. Extensive experiments on multiple public infrared benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative performance and visual quality, and further improves downstream infrared detection and segmentation tasks.

title: STRIDE: Continual Learning using Skill Transfer and Reuse with Incremental Discrete Encoding
abstract: Developing general-purpose physics-based character controllers via reinforcement learning is fundamentally hindered by policy interference in continuous spaces. While training isolated controllers avoids interference, it incurs significant training overhead and yields disjointed behavioral transitions. To address these challenges, we present STRIDE (Skill Transfer and Reuse with Incremental Discrete Encoding), a framework for the continual learning and composition of diverse character behaviors. Instead of training independent models, STRIDE leverages policy quantization via a Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQ-VAE) to dynamically discover and encode reusable behavioral primitives within a discrete latent space. New behaviors and tasks are learned by combining existing codewords, providing a stable motion prior that structurally eliminates catastrophic forgetting. Evaluated across diverse locomotion styles, agile maneuvers like kicking, and composite tasks like target-aiming, STRIDE accelerates downstream learning by × 1.3 to × 2.0 compared to baseline learning frameworks. Furthermore, the discrete representations inherently improve policy interpretability, allowing direct tracking of skill activations and behavioral decisions during task execution. STRIDE offers a scalable, transparent solution for continual character control without compromising motion quality.

title: A similarity-based approach for multi-dimensional classification
Information-guided rebalancing for multimodal classification
SFPrompt: Spatial-frequency dual prompting for lightweight all-in-one medical image restoration
abstract: Recently, all-in-one medical image restoration (MIR) has attracted increasing attention due to its ability to handle multiple types of degradations within a unified model. However, existing approaches often rely on auxiliary branches to extract degradation-aware priors, introducing additional model parameters. In addition, most methods primarily operate in the spatial domain and do not fully exploit frequency-domain differences between degraded and clean image pairs. To address these limitations, we propose SFPrompt, a parameter-efficient all-in-one MIR network that leverages prompt learning in both spatial and frequency domains. Specifically, the spatial prompt module extracts multi-scale degradation-related signals from intermediate features, while the frequency prompt module captures frequency-aware priors by exploiting the distinct properties of Fourier components. The extracted prompts are injected into the network via a dual-dimensional attention mechanism, thereby enhancing degradation adaptivity. We also develop a convolutional backbone that enhances multi-scale representations and higher-order feature interactions within a Transformer-style architecture. By integrating the proposed prompting strategy into this backbone, SFPrompt achieves a favorable trade-off between restoration quality and parameter count for CT image denoising, PET image synthesis, and MRI image super-resolution under both all-in-one and single-degradation settings.

title: Bridging theory and algorithm for Generalized Label Shift: An ambiguity perspective
SA-GIQA: A large-scale database and Semantic-Aware Generative Image Quality Assessment model
Resilient Transmission of Highly Structured Light via Active Convolved Illumination
abstract: Wave propagation through lossy and noisy systems as well as spatiotemporally dynamic random media often limits the complex information that can be reliably transmitted or retrieved. Progress in adaptive optics, wavefront shaping, machine learning, and wave propagation theories has significantly advanced physical and computational correction techniques. However, many approaches remain constrained by restrictive operating conditions, limiting their ability to meet growing application-specific demands, such as higher spatial resolution in imaging and greater data capacity in communications, particularly in highly dynamic environments. Recently, active convolved illumination (ACI) was proposed as a novel framework for preserving the spatial structure of optical modes during propagation through strongly distorting environments, such as atmospheric turbulence. ACI aims to bypass the prohibitive complexity of global distortion tracking by combining spectrally localized characterization with compensation using a correlated auxiliary source. Here, we provide a comprehensive review of ACI, detailing the formulation of correlation-injecting and auxiliary sources and the role of segmented reciprocal-space characterization and distortion compensation. We explore extensions in free-space optical communication and potential high-precision phase measurement, and numerically evaluate interferometric strategies for experimental implementation. This work highlights ACI as a potentially versatile framework for distortion-resilient light transmission, with broad interdisciplinary utility ranging from atmospheric physics and remote sensing to telecommunications, target tracking, and biomedical diagnosis, offering flexible deployment either as a standalone paradigm or hybridized with existing optical systems.

title: Characterization of Antarctic iceberg distributions using ICESat-2

A lightweight few-shot object detection framework using synthetic data augmentation for orchard obstacle recognition

title: A multi-sensor framework for comparing and integrating optical, C-band and L-band SAR inundation products in tropical floodplain of Australia
abstract: Accurate inundated landscape mapping is essential for understanding hydrological connectivity, wetland dynamics and floodplain processes in tropical environments. However, optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) sensors often produce inconsistent inundation estimates due to differences in sensor physics, wavelength sensitivity, vegetation and cloud penetration, and analytical methods. These challenges are amplified in wet–dry tropical systems, where cloud cover, heterogeneous vegetation and seasonal flooding complicate water detection. This study develops a unified multi-sensor framework for comparing and integrating inundation products derived from Sentinel-2 optical imagery, Sentinel-1 C-band and PALSAR-2 L-band SAR in the Daly River floodplain system in northern Australia. Inundated landscape maps were generated using supervised Random Forest classification and unsupervised multi-Otsu thresholding, followed by multi-sensor fusion analysis. Products were developed and validated using wet- and dry-season field observations and Indigenous Knowledges. Results showed strong seasonal and sensor-specific differences. Sentinel-2 provided the most balanced representation of dry-season floodplain vegetation and inundation, while Sentinel-1 achieved high wet-season overall accuracy (>0.95) under cloud-affected conditions. PALSAR-2 improved the detection of inundated vegetation and structurally complex environments, reaching an overall accuracy of 0.97. Multi-sensor evidential reasoning (fusion) improved spatial coherence and class delineation, but performance varied across sensor combinations. These findings show that optical, C-band SAR and L-band SAR inundation products are not directly interchangeable in tropical wetlands. Instead, they performed separately for each landscape. The proposed framework supports the comparison and integration of multi-sensor inundation products to enhance wetland conservation initiatives, wetland monitoring, hydrological assessment, and environmental management in data-limited tropical regions globally.

title: BathyUNet++ : a bathymetry retrieval framework for high-resolution low-SNR SuperDove imagery
abstract: High-spatial-resolution (HR) bathymetry is crucial for ensuring navigation safety and effective environmental management in shallow waters. However, traditional bathymetry retrieval from medium-resolution satellites yields large uncertainties under complex substrates and strong spatial heterogeneity. HR sensors, such as PlanetScope SuperDove (~3.7 m), can resolve fine-scale features but often have low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and limited spectral bands, leading to noisy bathymetry retrievals. To address this challenge, we developed BathyUNet++, a UNet++ architecture enhanced with spatial and channel squeeze & excitation (scSE) attention modules, for bathymetry retrieval from SuperDove imagery. While this architecture effectively leverages spatial context and complementary spectral information, it requires dense training patches. Traditional depth measurements provide sparse spatial coverage, and Airborne LiDAR Bathymetry (ALB) remains geographically limited. Therefore, we adopted a multi-source training strategy that integrates high-resolution ALB data with extensive Landsat 8/9 derived bathymetry to improve the spatial coverage and diversity of training data for SuperDove imagery. In addition, we designed a Central-Region Mean Squared Error (CMSE) that focuses on each patch's center valid receptive field to reduce instability and checkerboard artifacts often seen in satellite products generated via patch-based processing. Independent validation shows that BathyUNet++ achieves high-accuracy bathymetry retrievals, with median absolute percentage differences below 15% compared with independent depth measurements from ICESat-2 and ALB. Notably, BathyUNet++ substantially reduces noise compared with bathymetry maps derived from pixel-based algorithms, yielding spatially consistent bathymetry maps. The proposed framework overcomes the limitations of low-SNR data and can be readily adapted to other HR sensors, offering a promising solution for the broader application of HR bathymetry retrieval in optically shallow waters.

title: Vector Map as Language: Toward Unified Remote Sensing Vector Mapping
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Remote sensing vector mapping aims to generate structured maps of geospatial entities, such as buildings, roads, and water bodies, from remote sensing imagery. In practice, vector maps usually contain multiple category layers and heterogeneous entity structures, requiring a unified model for diverse mapping needs. However, existing methods typically represent vector objects as polygons or graphs, making them suitable only for specific categories: polygons poorly capture topological relations, while graphs often blur instance boundaries. We observe that language, as a natural medium for human communication, offers a flexible and expressive representation that can accommodate heterogeneous map elements, including geometry, semantics, and topology. Motivated by this insight, we propose Vector Map as Language (VecLang), a unified paradigm that reformulates multiclass vector mapping as structured text generation. VecLang encodes the common elements of different geospatial entities into a GeoJSON-like vector language, enabling cross-category modeling within a shared textual format. To generate this language reliably, we design a progressive vision-language mapping framework that first localizes vectorization units and then generates structured map elements. We further introduce Hierarchical Vector Language Optimization, which uses reinforcement learning to improve syntax validity, content fidelity, and map executability. We also build VecMap with 46k images and 800K instances, supporting training and evaluation across standard and generalization settings. Extensive experiments demonstrate that VecLang handles both single-class and multiclass vector mapping while achieving strong cross-dataset and open-vocabulary generalization.

title: TRUE: Towards Robust, Unique, and Efficient Model Fingerprint Generation and Verification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: While deep neural networks (DNNs) are being widely adopted, they are also increasingly exposed to model stealing risks, posing significant threats to intellectual property. Model fingerprinting, which utilizes intrinsic characteristics derived from the training process to authenticate models, has been proposed as a potential solution. An ideal fingerprint should satisfy robustness, uniqueness, and efficiency. However, existing methods often struggle to balance these three aspects simultaneously. To address this challenge, we propose TRUE, a twostage fingerprint generation and verification framework. In the fingerprint generation stage, we adopt adversarial examples as the fingerprint type and enhance their robustness through a minmax robust optimization strategy. In the fingerprint verification stage, we assign weights to the adversarial examples using a Boltzmann distribution to reflect their uniqueness, and further employ sampling based on these weights to reduce the number of queries and improve efficiency. Extensive experiments conducted on real-world datasets and across different model architectures demonstrate the superiority of the TRUE framework.

title: HPS-MVC: Hierarchical Pseudo-Supervised Multi-View Clustering
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Existing pseudo-supervised multi-view clustering methods typically utilize pseudo-supervision at a single semantic level, which fails to capture the intrinsic structure of complex data and thus restricts clustering performance. We propose Hierarchical Pseudo-Supervised Multi-View Clustering (HPS-MVC), which leverages multi-level semantic pseudo-supervision signals to guide the clustering process. Specifically, hierarchical pseudo-supervision signals are constructed by mining sample neighborhood relations and are then used to aggregate samples at different semantic levels as inputs to an anchor-based multi-view clustering model. A dual-weighting strategy is further introduced to select high-quality anchor graphs for optimal graph fusion. An efficient alternating optimization algorithm is developed to solve the resulting problem. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness, efficiency, and scalability of the proposed method.

title: Contextual Chamfer Distance for Point Cloud Restoration
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Accurate similarity measurement between point clouds is crucial for 3D geometry restoration. Chamfer Distance (CD) and its variants quantify such similarity in a permutation-invariant manner, yet they emphasize low-order point-wise proximity, leading to clustered distributions and long-range structural distortions that undermine geometric fidelity. This work rethinks point cloud similarity from a high-order standpoint and introduces Contextual Chamfer Distance (CCD), a geometrically consistent formulation that jointly models point-wise proximity, local distribution consistency, and long-range structural consistency. Specifically, Patch Density Consistency (PDC) aligns relative patch densities between predicted and ground-truth points, promoting spatial coverage for geometric completeness, while Anchor Normal Consistency (ANC) models long-range relationships through anchor normals derived from non-degenerate point triplets, improving structural coherence and geometric accuracy. Alongside this formulation, we develop a conditional local coordinate-space stability and convergence analysis and derive sufficient conditions for local linear convergence of the corresponding weighted objective under explicit local assumptions. Extensive experiments on completion, compression, and upsampling across architectures and six datasets demonstrate consistent quantitative and qualitative gains across settings, a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off, and strong generalization.

title: Towards Robust Multi-View Clustering via Early-to-late Manifold Consistency Calibration
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: For multi-view data, structural heterogeneity across views is a common property, with cross-view sparsity variation serving as a typical manifestation. To first account for this sparsity-induced heterogeneity, we develop Adaptive View-specific Encoding, which incorporates the sparsity ratio of each view as prior knowledge for view-aware representation learning and constraint modulation. Based thereon, we further tackle the broader issue of view quality imbalance in multi-view fusion, where low-quality views introduce unreliable structural relations and view-specific constraints further amplify latent discrepancies. To this end, we propose a globallocal manifold-guided fusion mechanism named Early-to-late Manifold Consistency Calibration, which leverages the relatively stable global manifold preserved in early-fused encoded features to modulate robust late-stage fusion of adaptively encoded local features. Specifically, the early-stage global features serve as a structural anchor for assessing the manifold consistency of features of each adaptively encoded local view. The resulting consistency scores are then used to adaptively reweight late-stage global fusion, attenuating structurally unreliable views while reinforcing those aligned with the common manifold. In this manner, latent manifold consistency enables early fusion to calibrate late-stage fusion, thereby establishing a principled connection between adaptive view-specific encoding and cross-view distribution alignment. The full framework, named Manifold Consistency Guided Adaptive Sparse Autoencoder for Multiview Clustering (MASA), is validated on multiple datasets and demonstrates superior effectiveness and robustness across diverse experimental settings. On ALOI-100, MASA further enhances clustering stability, reducing the fluctuation standard deviation over the final rounds from 3.02% to 1.28%.

title: Bridging the Training Gap with Hyperion: A Training-Free Style Transfer Method on Diffusion Transformers
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Training-free style transfer on Multimodal Diffusion Transformers (MM-DiT) remains challenging due to the persistent gap between trained adapters and injection-based training-free methods. Existing training-free methods typically perform forward feature injection, and thus struggle to reproduce the rich painterly textures achieved by trained adapters, often leading to only faint hue shifts. In this paper, we trace this limitation to the absence of backpropagation-induced spatial coupling and propose Hyperion, a fully training-free style-transfer pipeline for MM-DiT. At the optimization level, the pipeline introduces Adam-in-loop, which iteratively optimizes the diffusion latent at each denoising step with a frozen MM-DiT. This process recovers the gradient-driven coupling effect produced through the self-attention value path, where neighboring tokens receive highly similar updates and form coherent brushstroke textures. At the distribution level, the pipeline introduces Sinkhorn Latent Transport (SLT), a single closed-form optimal-transport step that pre-aligns latent color distributions before Adam optimization, improving the operational efficiency of Adam-in-loop. To further enhance stylization quality, we develop a frequency-domain Sinkhorn loss to sharpen painterly textures and a layout-residual-suppression step to reduce layout interference. The pipeline can also be extended to image-to-image stylization. Extensive experiments on a 39-style × 6-prompt benchmark (234 pairs) demonstrate that Hyperion achieves CSD $= 0.640$ and CLIP-T $= 0.296$, improving CSD by +5.2% over Adam-8 at $2.5\times$ lower forward-pass cost and by +16.6% over Adam-only under an equal compute budget. Notably, Hyperion outperforms four pre-trained style adapters on 19 of 21 diverse style families, achieving a mean CSD of 0.657 versus 0.506 for the strongest baseline.

title: Expediting Pre-training for Vision Transformers Through Hierarchical Data Sparsity Optimization
abstract: Pre-training cost is a crucial problem in the era of the emerging large models. This is mainly caused by high model computation complexity and the million-scale training datasets, which require extensive time to train from scratch. The substantial training cost associated with recent models poses a significant barrier for individuals and institutions with limited resources. This not only impedes their ability to reach or exceed cutting-edge advancements but also restricts the practical deployment and application of these models on resource-limited devices. Most compression algorithms focus only on efficient fine-tuning or inference from the pre-trained dense models, while time-consuming pre-training is still unavoidable. In contrast, this paper points out that training data is redundant, which is the fundamental reason for the tedious training. To address the issue, this paper aims to introduce sparsity into data and proposes an end-to-end approach for pre-training acceleration by exploiting data redundancy from three sparse perspectives, dubbed Tri-Level ViT++ . Specifically, we leverage a hierarchical reduction scheme by exploring the data sparsity under three levels: the number of training samples in the dataset, the number of patches (tokens) in each sample, and the number of connections between tokens that lie in attention weights. With extensive experiments, we demonstrate that our proposed technique can noticeably accelerate both pre-training and inference for various ViT architectures while maintaining accuracy. Remarkably, under certain ratios, we are able to improve the ViT accuracy rather than compromising it. For example, we can achieve 22.3% speedup with 73.0% (+0.8) Top-1 accuracy on Deit-T, and 22.5% speedup with 80.1% (+0.3) Top-1 accuracy on Deit-S. This proves the existence of data redundancy in ViT.

title: Spatial-Frequency-Aware Implicit Neural Representation of Multidimensional Signals via MLP-KAN Fusion
abstract: Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) have emerged as a compelling paradigm for modeling multidimensional signals by mapping continuous coordinates to signal values. However, Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLP)-based INRs inherently suffer from spectral bias, which favors low-frequency components and suppresses the reconstruction of essential high-frequency details. While existing techniques, such as Fourier feature mappings, mitigate this issue, they often rely on sensitive manual tuning and are prone to spectral artifacts. In this paper, we propose a spatial-frequency-aware INR framework that combines an MLP branch with a Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN) branch for complementary frequency-oriented modeling. The MLP branch provides a low-frequency-oriented representation of smooth structures, whereas the KAN branch complements localized variations and fine details. To coordinate the two branches, we integrate the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and inverse discrete wavelet transform (IDWT) into the output fusion stage. The outputs of the two branches are decomposed into wavelet coefficients, and the corresponding coefficients are additively fused before inverse wavelet reconstruction. A wavelet-domain band-separation regularization further penalizes high-frequency responses in the MLP branch and low-frequency responses in the KAN branch, thereby encouraging complementary frequency-oriented behavior. Experiments on 1D signals, 2D images, 3D volumes and signed distance functions, videos, and 4D light-fields demonstrate the applicability of the proposed representation across the evaluated signal modalities. Results demonstrate improved reconstruction fidelity across the evaluated signal modalities.

title: Progressive Style Transfer for Exemplar-based Open-world Sketch Colorization
abstract: Sketch colorization in open-world scenarios presents unique challenges due to diverse, unpaired datasets and the variety in user-generated sketch styles. Traditional exemplar-based methods, which typically rely on dense feature matching and style normalization, struggle to generalize effectively in these conditions, as they require structured paired data and exhibit limited flexibility. We introduce Progressive Style Transfer (PROST), a completely unsupervised framework that addresses these limitations by progressively injecting style features into sketches without rigid content-style alignment. PROST comprises two key modules: Progressive Style Injection (PSI), which transfers style features adaptively across scales, and Progressive Style Enhancement (PSE), which refines style coherence through multi-layer style-adaptive attention. Together, these modules enable flexible style transfer that preserves content fidelity while achieving high stylistic coherence. Our approach also integrates a Dual Cycle-Consistency (DCC) framework to ensure both style and content consistency in generated outputs. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that PROST effectively generalizes to unseen styles, achieving robust performance across varied datasets and setting a new benchmark for open-world sketch colorization. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Vincotto/ProST.

title: Preserving Structural Irreplaceability in Token Pruning through Local Representation Complexity
abstract: The effectiveness of vision token pruning critically depends on the criterion used to define token redundancy. Existing approaches, which primarily rely on global saliency scores or similarity heuristics, often fail to account for a token's essential contribution to the model's internal representations. This oversight results in retaining visually prominent but redundant tokens or merging semantically distinct features, severely degrading performance under tight compression budgets. To address this, we propose a novel token pruning strategy aligned with representation complexity. We first introduce Local Representation Complexity (LRC), a token-level measure that estimates the intrinsic dimension of each token's embedding. Tokens exhibiting high LRC are considered locally unpredictable and are therefore prioritized for preservation. To ensure selection diversity and mitigate over-concentration in the selected set, we frame the pruning process as a budget allocation problem and introduce a Greedy Selection algorithm with Penalized Diversity to actively suppress redundancy. We evaluate the proposed method across five vision-language model backbones from three model families, including LLaVA-1.5/LLaVA-NeXT, Qwen2.5-VL/Qwen3-VL, and InternVL3, covering a wide range of capacities and tasks. The results demonstrate competitive performance across different backbones, with particularly notable gains at aggressive compression ratios.
